author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
Trump again congratulated Ohio senator’s rear end before his cheeky comment about rapper being ‘hard to miss’

Donald Trump reiterated his apparent love for buxom bums during a rally in Michigan on Sunday where he encouraged the crowd to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj’s behind.

Trump’s cheeky comments about Minaj’s derriere came as he explained his recent observation on the Republican Ohio senator Jon Husted’s rear end. Earlier in October, Trump said of the former college football player: “I don’t do this with men very often. I started examining his body, because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I
title: Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan

author: Kat Wong
description:
Follow live updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

UTI treatment, contraception to be available through pharmacies

All Australian women will soon be able to attend a pharmacy for UTI treatment or re-supply of hormonal contraception, as the federal government expands a trial program to lower health care costs.

For too long, women’s experiences of the health system haven’t received the attention they deserve. We’re determined to change that. We’re making practical changes that give women more choice, make health care more accessible and help save women thousands of dollars over their lifetimes.

We want to make it easier for women to get care that fits into their lives.<
title: Australia politics live: MPs to pay tribute to Helen Haines as parliament resumes; Hanson says One Nation cartoons ‘not going anywhere’

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Chancellor is in favour the North Sea project, but energy secretary has said she is leaning towards rejecting it

A cabinet split has emerged over whether to approve drilling at the Rosebank oilfield, with the chancellor, John Healey, in favour of the controversial North Sea project.

The energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, is ultimately in charge of the decision and the Guardian reported last week that she was leaning towards rejecting it after granting permission for the smaller Jackdaw gasfield.

Continue reading...
title: Cabinet split emerges over controversial Rosebank oilfield decision

author: Coral Murphy Marcos and agencies
description:
Peltola and her family sustained minor injuries after a driver struck the car transporting group to campaign stop

Mary Peltola, a Democrat who is running for Alaska’s lone US Senate seat, and her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash while driving to a campaign stop on Saturday, her campaign said.

The family was on its way to the Alaska Federation of Natives annual banquet when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, her campaign said in a statement on Sunday. Peltola required medical attention after the collision.

Continue reading...
title: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crash

author: Seán Clarke and Tom Phillips
description:
After a shock defeat in the first round, the incumbent Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is seeking a new term in a runoff with Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of his convicted predecessor

Polls were originally due to close at 17.00BRT, 20.00GMT, but voting has been extended for two hours; some districts had already counted. Full coverage here

Continue reading...
title: Brazil election 2026: Live second round results

author: Ashifa Kassam and agencies
description:
More than 30 people arrested as officers clear at least 100 tents in central Lisbon and about 50 in Porto

Police in Portugal have dismantled housing protest camps in Lisbon and Porto, baton-charging campaigners in the early hours of Sunday and arresting more than 30 people.

The raids were the latest incident in days of clashes between police and campaigners who – inspired by similar camps in Spain – had sought to pitch tents in central squares to protest against the country’s deepening housing crisis.

Continue reading...
title: Police in Portugal ‘use dogs and batons’ to dismantle housing protest camps

author: Jessica Glenza
description:
Man accused of shooting teen, who was driving to a party, has also been linked to shooting of a vehicle days earlier

A man accused in the shooting death of a Missouri teen has been charged in a second shooting incident – both of which involve firing into cars on the highway.

Alyssa Wilson, 17, was shot and killed as she drove down Interstate 170 in Overland, Missouri, on 14 October. The teen was on her way to a Halloween party at St Louis Zoo, called Boo at the Zoo, when a suspect fired a single shot into the back of Wilson’s Buick Encore.

Continue reading...
title: Suspect in shooting death of teen on Missouri highway charged in second road incident

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
Exclusive: RACGP survey reflects Medicare investments, but experts caution quality of care and outcomes also matter

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The proportion of general practitioners bulk-billing all of their patients has more than doubled in a year, a report has found, after the government introduced financial incentives for doctors and practices.

And almost two-thirds (63%) of Australians are now bulk-billed for all their GP care, up from 56% in both 2024 and 2025, which the report says is “likely a reflection of the federal government’s recent investment in Medicare bulk billing incentives”.
title: Almost two-thirds of Australians bulk-billed for all GP care amid extra incentives for doctors

author: Krishani Dhanji and Josh Taylor
description:
State paid consultancy firm $166,000 for feasibility study on merging the three tertiary institutions

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Western Australian government has said it is “extremely disappointed” and is seeking an “expedited” cost recovery from Deloitte after errors were discovered in a report about a potential university merger, including AI-hallucinated references and hundreds of millions of dollars in cost discrepancies.

The government paid Deloitte $166,000 for a feasibility study on merging the University of Western Australia, Curtin University and Murdoch University.

Continu
title: ‘Extremely disappointed’: WA government seeks reimbursement from Deloitte over flawed university report

author: Dani Anguiano in Shasta county
description:
Shasta has embraced the Maga movement with gusto – can Democrats ever win back the rural, working-class voters they once relied upon?

A crucial election was approaching and the country was desperate. Despite promises that economic conditions were improving, nearly a quarter of the US was out of work as voters headed to the polls in 1932.

It was the darkest time since the civil war, a period so dire that in California’s capital people fought each other for work. In early 1931, a crowd of 200 men scuffled over a handful of temporary jobs moving back-breaking loads of granite, the Sacramento Bee reported.

Continue reading...
title: FDR made it a blue bastion – now it’s Trump’s stronghold in California. Is it forever lost?

author: Ben Quinn and Jessica Elgot
description:
Sources close to Tory leader say Jack Ross, who faces party investigation after undercover report, worked as social media consultant

A former Conservative election candidate who was suspended after he was filmed discussing the cost of hiring contract killers worked as a consultant in Kemi Badenoch’s office as recently as last year.

Jack Ross is facing an investigation by the Tories after he was filmed apparently asking an undercover reporter: “What do you want done?” and apparently offering to “broker” the services of an alleged far-right paramilitary group.

Continue reading...
title: Former Tory candidate suspended over contract killer claims was adviser in Kemi Badenoch’s office

author: Graeme Wearden
description:
Experts say Bank of England unlikely to increase rates by full percentage point – and could lower them by end of 2027

Financial markets are wrong to predict the Bank of England will raise UK interest rates by a full percentage point or more by next summer, City economists believe.

According to market-implied interest rate expectations, the Bank is likely to raise interest rates at least four times over the next year, lifting the bank rate from 3.75% today to 4.75% by the end of July, and possibly to 5% – meaning five rises – by December 2027.

Continue reading...
title: Interest rates unlikely to reach 4.75% by next summer, say City economists

author: Tom Perkins
description:
This gives the company an advantage in tracking objects in orbit, raising national security concerns and fears of greater control over the space industry

The US military has given Elon Musk’s SpaceX access to restricted space tracking data, raising a new round of questions about whether the Trump administration is attempting to hand over traffic control in Earth’s orbit to a controversial donor.

The access also raises new national security questions, industry observers say.

Continue reading...
title: US military gives Elon Musk’s SpaceX access to sensitive tracking data

author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
description:
Irish and Welsh authors Chris Haughton and Nicola Davies show solidarity over Rooney’s support for Palestine Action

The children’s laureates for Ireland and Wales are donating royalties from their works to Sally Rooney in a show of solidarity after she was forced to stop selling books in the UK because of her support for Palestine Action.

Chris Haughton, Ireland’s children’s literature laureate, said he also wanted to demonstrate the “absurdity” of the bestselling author being unable to receive royalties from her own UK sales because of her public support for the direct action group.

Continue reading...
title: Two children’s laureates to give Sally Rooney royalties after ban on UK sales

author: Eric Berger
description:
Stakeholders concerned more people at risk of food insecurity after One Big Beautiful Act took effect

Enrollment in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Snap) has decreased significantly over the past year in the US following restrictions imposed by the Trump administration, which has forced more people to seek help from food banks or go hungry, stakeholders say.

The number of people who receive food stamps has dropped from 41.6 million in July 2025, before the One Big Beautiful Act took effect, to 36.5 million in June 2026, a 13% decrease, according to the latest data from the US Department of Agriculture, which administers the program.

Continue reading...
title: Trump administration has pushed off 13% of Americans enrolled in food stamps

author: Simon Goodley
description:
Andrew Woosnam took millions from his recruitment firms before creditors, including HMRC, were left out of pocket

  • Companies revived in ‘phoenix’ deals more likely to fail, study finds

For three decades, the recruitment industry treated Andrew Woosnam well.

Having learned his trade during the 1990s, he graduated to create his own firm at the turn of the millennium – which allowed him to bank millions of pounds in salary, dividends and loans and to buy assets including a grand house in Berkshire once owned by the comedians Dawn French and Lenny Henry.

Continue reading...
title: The boss whose twice-bust business appears to be back despite £3m debts

author: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent
description:
BoM predicts hail, damaging winds, flash flooding and power outages across southern Queensland, western NSW, the ACT and eastern Victoria on Sunday afternoon

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Large parts of eastern Australia were put on alert for severe thunderstorms on Sunday afternoon with more potential storms and flood risk in store for Monday.

On Sunday afternoon, the Bureau of Meteorology issued a severe thunderstorm warning for Sydney, greater Wollongong and parts of Blue Mountains, Hawkesbury, Gosford, Wyong and Wollondilly, Wingecarribee areas.

Continue re
title: ‘Unusually large’ multi-state storm causing severe weather for Australia’s east – with more on the way

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Commissioner Krissy Barrett says women are more often singled out, often with threats of sexual violence

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s top federal law enforcement official has drawn a direct link between politicians’ rhetoric and threats and abuse being directed at leaders.

The safety of elected representatives at all levels has been thrown into the spotlight after independent MP Helen Haines was allegedly deliberate attacked outside her Wangaratta electoral office.

Continue reading...
title: AFP boss says politicians’ heated rhetoric is fuelling threats against MPs

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
State attorney general said Trump’s justice department’s directive to verify 20,000 ballots is completely improper

California’s attorney general on Saturday rebuked the Trump administration’s efforts to quash alleged noncitizen voting, calling it “politicizing and weaponizing the law”.

Rob Bonta, the state’s attorney general, said the justice department acted at Donald Trump’s direction.

Continue reading...
title: California leader calls attack on alleged noncitizen voting ‘weaponizing the law’
